user_sees: units lost to follow-up (`c`) contribute the time points they were seen, so the risks are those had no unit been lost, assuming loss depends only on the measured history
notes: Contradicts S7-063's wording for the same rows. The declared censoring column is not used by the g-formula's models.

statement: sd(r_i)/√n_sim over the simulated units' final risks bounds the g-formula's Monte Carlo error from above.
decision: the methods text's Monte Carlo error
user_sees: (Monte Carlo error at most 0.0040)
notes: With n_sim equal to the units, sd(r_i) includes between-unit variation, so it is an upper bound; with a resampled base it is about the Monte Carlo SE itself. The sentence reports the larger of always and never (stages/time_varying.py:1026).

statement: Comparing the natural course's simulated risk with the observed (nonparametric) cumulative risk checks the g-formula's models.
decision: the natural-course curve and methods text
user_sees: The natural course's simulated risk was compared with the observed risk as a check of the models.
notes: The observed risk assumes loss is independent of the outcome (models/time_varying.py:671-678); no threshold or warning is attached to a disagreement.

statement: Regression calibration from repeated 24-hour recalls corrects only within-person random (day-to-day) error and assumes the recalls are unbiased for usual intake; because recalls share each person's reporting bias, using the 24HR as the reference can seriously underestimate true attenuation.
regime: inference; regression calibration with 24-h recalls as the replicate measure
decision: label stated with every calibrated result
user_sees: "corrects only within-person random error, assuming recalls are unbiased for usual intake (customary; sound under that assumption)"
claimed_basis: Kipnis et al. 2003 (Am J Epidemiol 158:14) 'can seriously underestimate true attenuation (up to 60% for energy-adjusted protein)'
notes: Docstring calibration.py:75-79. Label attached to every option's 'sound' text.

statement: For a logistic (or proportional-odds) outcome model, substituting the calibrated exposure E[X | W, Z] for the error-prone one is an approximation (adequate when the outcome is rare or the measurement error small), not an exact correction.
regime: inference; regression calibration with a binary or ordinal outcome
user_sees: "For a logistic or proportional-odds outcome, substituting the calibrated score is an approximation (Carroll et al. 2006, §4.2)."
notes: Also calibration.py:39-40 and methods/scales.py:67-70. The app does not state the rare-outcome/small-error condition; the parenthetical in the statement is the standard regime, added by the inventory (see Carroll §4.2). turbotab/core/tests/acceptance/test_wp12c_calibration.py::test_6_for_a_logistic_model_the_calibration_is_the_usual_approximation checks the computation, not the adequacy.

statement: A reliability estimated from internal consistency (α or ω) omits transient (occasion-specific) error, so a correction based on it under-corrects, whereas a test-retest repeat administration includes transient error.
decision: label on corrections from internal consistency; ranking of test-retest above ω
user_sees: "A reliability from internal consistency omits transient error, so the correction under-corrects (Schmidt, Le & Ilies 2003)."
claimed_basis: Schmidt, Le & Ilies 2003 (Psychol Methods 8:206); MODELING_SEQUENCE §0 ruling 8
notes: Also methods/scales.py:111-114 and the methods sentence core/scales.py:1008-1010. Ranking effect: rc_test_retest 'recommended', rc_internal_consistency 'available' (core/scales.py:128-145), so it is partly tier 1.

regime: inference; >=2 scale scores in the model, only some corrected
user_sees: "... is also a scale score in the model, entered uncorrected, so this correction reads it as measured without error; with two or more error-prone study factors, estimates 'may become attenuated, infl…
notes: Companion of the multivariate-calibration claim.

statement: Which scale items are reverse-coded must come from the instrument's published key and cannot be inferred from the data, because a negative item-rest correlation has four indistinguishable explanations (needs reversing, already reversed, method factor, does not belong).
user_sees: Nothing inferred; user declares reversed items
notes: Design rule in a docstring; governs that the app never proposes reversals.
